**Run Large Language Models on Your Own Hardware with llama.cpp**

Ever wanted to run a powerful AI model on your own laptop or desktop without relying on cloud APIs? Meet `llama.cpp`, an open-source project that makes large language model (LLM) inference accessible to everyone. Built entirely in C/C++, it strips away heavy dependencies, focusing on speed, efficiency, and minimal setup. Whether you’re a developer, a tinkerer, or just curious about AI, this tool puts state-of-the-art intelligence right on your machine.

What makes `llama.cpp` special? It’s incredibly versatile. It supports a massive range of hardware, from Apple Silicon Macs (with optimized Metal support) to NVIDIA GPUs (via CUDA), AMD GPUs (via HIP), and even Intel CPUs and NPUs. It doesn’t just run on high-end gaming rigs; it’s optimized for efficiency, allowing you to run large models on modest hardware by using quantization techniques. This means you can shrink model sizes by up to 80% with minimal loss in quality, making it feasible to run 7B or even 13B parameter models on consumer-grade devices.
